slides.text: When the weeping specter of a nineteenth-century sea captain began floating three feet above our front hydrangeas at 3:00 AM, my wife wanted to call a priest. I told her to wait until 7:00 AM. Sure enough, at 7:02, Linda—the undefeated tyrant of the Whispering Pines Homeowners Association—marched up our driveway armed with a laminated clipboard, a laser tape measure, and a high-visibility vest.

'Excuse me!' Linda barked directly into the swirling vortex of damned souls. 'Section 4, Paragraph B of the community bylaws strictly prohibits unapproved lawn ornaments, fog machines, or nautical apparitions visible from the cul-de-sac!' The ghost rattled his ethereal chains and howled, 'I AM CAPTAIN EZEKIEL, CURSED TO DROWN IN ETERNAL SORROW!' Linda didn't even blink. She clicked her ballpoint pen.

'Well, Captain Ezekiel, your eternal sorrow is currently a non-compliant shade of ectoplasmic teal. Approved exterior colors are Eggshell, Sandstone, and Muted Taupe. That’s a two-hundred-dollar fine per night, plus late fees.' The ghost stared at her clipboard, looked at his translucent hands, and muttered, 'Wait, compounded daily?' He vanished into the afterlife on the spot and hasn't haunted the zip code since.
